summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct public-company universe for restaurant labor productivity and kitchen operating automation. The strongest direct equipment exposure is Middleby, with ITW as a large-cap reference anchor. The underfollowed lane includes PAR Technology for restaurant operating software/POS and TransAct Technologies as a speculative micro-cap back-of-house automation and food-safety workflow vendor. The main chokepoint hypothesis remains that chain-approved equipment, installed bases, serviceability, and workflow integration may matter more than futuristic restaurant robotics. Expanded the universe for restaurant labor-productivity and uptime chokepoints around chain-approved equipment, beverage systems, restaurant operating software, coffee/beverage service infrastructure, and early-stage robotics. The highest-quality reference exposure is Middleby because it directly manufactures commercial foodservice cooking, refrigeration, beverage, IoT and robotics-related equipment. The underfollowed lane is more interesting in PAR Technology and Farmer Brothers: PAR maps to enterprise restaurant POS/back-office/labor/ordering workflows, while Farmer Brothers is a micro-cap speculative exception with coffee, beverage, equipment service and route density exposure. Richtech Robotics is included only as a speculative_shadow candidate because it is directly tied to restaurant/hospitality robots but has weak proof quality, small-company execution risk, and controversy risk.
